candidates.text:
`JsonSchemaTransformer` skips `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` members when the node also has a `type`

### Initial Checks

- [x] I'm using the latest version of Pydantic AI (reproduced on `main` @ `3adb9b0`).
- [x] I've searched the issue tracker before opening this.

### Description

`JsonSchemaTransformer._handle` only recurses into `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` members when the node has no `type`:

```python
# pydantic_ai/_json_schema.py
elif type_ is None:
    schema = self._handle_union(schema, 'allOf')
    schema = self._handle_union(schema, 'anyOf')
    schema = self._handle_union(schema, 'oneOf')
```

`allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` are independent applicators: a node can legally carry both a `type` and one of them, and such nodes show up in practice via user-provided and MCP tool `inputSchema`s. When that happens, `_handle_object`/`_handle_array` recurse `properties`/`items` but never the composition members, so those members (and their nested subschemas) are never walked and `transform` is never applied to them. Provider transformers then leave provider-incompatible keys in place inside the members.

This is the same root family as #6394 (which added `allOf` recursion for the typeless case); it just is not reached when the node also has a `type`.

Invariant: every subschema in the tree should be visited by `transform` exactly once; `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` can co-exist with `type`.

### Minimal, Reproducible Example

Offline, no network or provider call:

```python
from pydantic_ai.profiles.google import GoogleJsonSchemaTransformer

schema = {
    'type': 'object',
    'properties': {'p': {'type': 'string'}},
    'anyOf': [
        {'type': 'integer', 'title': 'Count', 'exclusiveMinimum': 0},
    ],
}
out = GoogleJsonSchemaTransformer(schema).walk()
print(out['anyOf'][0])
# actual  : {'type': 'integer', 'title': 'Count', 'exclusiveMinimum': 0}
# expected: {'type': 'integer'}
```

Explore an MCP server for QCobro

## Summary
Investigate exposing QCobro's capabilities via a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so AI agents/tools can interact with the platform programmatically.

## Problem / Motivation
QCobro already has a solid, well-typed API (tRPC over `mods/apiserver`, contracts shared via `mods/common`). As AI agents (including coding/ops agents) and external tooling increasingly rely on MCP as the standard way to interact with services, QCobro currently has no MCP surface — any agent-driven workflow (querying campaigns, contacts, payment promises, gestiones, or triggering outreach) requires bespoke integration instead of a discoverable, standard interface.

## Proposed Solution
Explore wrapping/exposing existing tRPC procedures as MCP tools/resources. Key open questions to research:
- **Architecture**: where the MCP server would live (new `mods/mcp` package vs. a thin layer in `mods/apiserver`) and how it reuses `mods/common` schemas/types rather than duplicating contracts.
- **Auth model**: introduce a dedicated, limited-permission role/scope (via Fonoster Identity) for MCP access, distinct from full operator permissions, so agent-driven actions are scoped down by default (e.g. read-only or a narrow allowlist of mutations).
- **Scope of exposed operations**: which are safe to expose first (read-heavy: contacts, campaigns, payment promises, gestiones) vs. which are too risky for unsupervised agent-initiated writes (e.g. dispatching outreach, marking payments paid).

- **Multi-tenancy**: whether this is a single general MCP server or workspace-scoped, given QCobro's multi-tenant model.

- [ ] Recommendation on architecture (where it lives, how it reuses the existing API/schemas

```python
    'anyOf': [
```

candidates.text:
`JsonSchemaTransformer` skips `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` members when the node also has a `type`

### Initial Checks

- [x] I'm using the latest version of Pydantic AI (reproduced on `main` @ `3adb9b0`).
- [x] I've searched the issue tracker before opening this.

### Description

`JsonSchemaTransformer._handle` only recurses into `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` members when the node has no `type`:

```python
# pydantic_ai/_json_schema.py
elif type_ is None:
    schema = self._handle_union(schema, 'allOf')
    schema = self._handle_union(schema, 'anyOf')
    schema = self._handle_union(schema, 'oneOf')
```

`allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` are independent applicators: a node can legally carry both a `type` and one of them, and such nodes show up in practice via user-provided and MCP tool `inputSchema`s. When that happens, `_handle_object`/`_handle_array` recurse `properties`/`items` but never the composition members, so those members (and their nested subschemas) are never walked and `transform` is never applied to them. Provider transformers then leave provider-incompatible keys in place inside the members.

This is the same root family as #6394 (which added `allOf` recursion for the typeless case); it just is not reached when the node also has a `type`.

Invariant: every subschema in the tree should be visited by `transform` exactly once; `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` can co-exist with `type`.

### Minimal, Reproducible Example

Offline, no network or provider call:

```python
from pydantic_ai.profiles.google import GoogleJsonSchemaTransformer

schema = {
    'type': 'object',
    'properties': {'p': {'type': 'string'}},
    'anyOf': [
        {'type': 'integer', 'title': 'Count', 'exclusiveMinimum': 0},
    ],
}
out = GoogleJsonSchemaTransformer(schema).walk()
print(out['anyOf'][0])
# actual  : {'type': 'integer', 'title': 'Count', 'exclusiveMinimum': 0}
# expected: {'type': 'integer'}
```

source_metadata.title: Support per-tool strict schema passthrough in defineTool

candidates.text:
Support per-tool strict schema passthrough in defineTool

### What problem are you trying to solve?

The AI SDK supports a per-tool `strict?: boolean` flag for function tools, and OpenAI-compatible providers can forward it as `tools[].function.strict`. Eve currently has no public or compiled representation for that flag:

- `ToolDefinition` / `PublicToolDefinition` do not expose `strict`.
- `InternalToolDefinition` and `CompiledToolDefinition` do not carry it.
- The compiled manifest schema has no `strict` field for tools.

As a result, an authored Eve tool cannot opt into provider-native strict tool calling. Adding `strict: true` behind a cast is not sufficient because the compiler/runtime boundary does not preserve the field.

Minimal API shape that is currently unavailable:

```ts
import { defineTool } from "eve/tools";
import { z } from "zod";

export default defineTool({
  description: "Get weather for a city.",
  inputSchema: z.object({ city: z.string() }),
  strict: true,
  execute({ city }) {
    return { city, temperatureC: 24 };
  },
});
```

This matters for providers that offer schema-constrained function calling. DeepSeek's strict tool mode, for example, requires `strict: true` on every function in the request and validates all submitted JSON Schemas before generation:

https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/tool_calls/

Without an Eve-level pass-through, applications must maintain a patch/fork, bypass Eve's harness, or give up provider-guaranteed argument conformance. This also needs to cover Eve framework tools: a provider that requires every function to be strict cannot be supported by forwarding the field only for authored tools.

This is separate from #542. That proposal makes invalid tool calls observable; this request allows providers to prevent schema-invalid arguments during generation.

Observed on `eve@0.22.4`; I also inspected the published `eve@0.22.6` types and manifest schema and did not find a strict-tool field.

source_metadata.title: `JsonSchemaTransformer` skips `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` members when the node also has a `type`

candidates.text:
`JsonSchemaTransformer` skips `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` members when the node also has a `type`

### Initial Checks

- [x] I'm using the latest version of Pydantic AI (reproduced on `main` @ `3adb9b0`).
- [x] I've searched the issue tracker before opening this.

### Description

`JsonSchemaTransformer._handle` only recurses into `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` members when the node has no `type`:

```python
# pydantic_ai/_json_schema.py
elif type_ is None:
    schema = self._handle_union(schema, 'allOf')
    schema = self._handle_union(schema, 'anyOf')
    schema = self._handle_union(schema, 'oneOf')
```

`allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` are independent applicators: a node can legally carry both a `type` and one of them, and such nodes show up in practice via user-provided and MCP tool `inputSchema`s. When that happens, `_handle_object`/`_handle_array` recurse `properties`/`items` but never the composition members, so those members (and their nested subschemas) are never walked and `transform` is never applied to them. Provider transformers then leave provider-incompatible keys in place inside the members.

This is the same root family as #6394 (which added `allOf` recursion for the typeless case); it just is not reached when the node also has a `type`.

Invariant: every subschema in the tree should be visited by `transform` exactly once; `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` can co-exist with `type`.

### Minimal, Reproducible Example

Offline, no network or provider call:

```python
from pydantic_ai.profiles.google import GoogleJsonSchemaTransformer

schema = {
    'type': 'object',
    'properties': {'p': {'type': 'string'}},
    'anyOf': [
        {'type': 'integer', 'title': 'Count', 'exclusiveMinimum': 0},
    ],
}
out = GoogleJsonSchemaTransformer(schema).walk()
print(out['anyOf'][0])
# actual  : {'type': 'integer', 'title': 'Count', 'exclusiveMinimum': 0}
# expected: {'type': 'integer'}
```

Azure OpenAI Responses (store:false) still 400s on multi-turn reasoning replay in 0.80.3 (bare rs_ id, no encrypted_content backfill)

### What happened?

Multi-turn conversations against `azure-openai-responses` reasoning models fail on the follow-up turn with:

```
400 Item with id 'rs_...' not found. Items are not persisted when store is set to false.
Try again with store set to true, or remove this item from your input.
```

This is the same class of failure as #4272 (Azure; closed as `closed-because-bigrefactor`, with fix PR #4256 never merged) and the OpenAI-side #3369 / #5059. It **still reproduces on 0.80.3 / current main** — the refactor did not close the Azure path.

**Root cause (code-grounded, 0.80.3):**

`packages/ai/src/api/openai-responses-shared.ts` → `convertResponsesMessages()` replays the captured reasoning item verbatim, including its server-side `rs_` id:

```js
if (block.type === "thinking") {
    if (block.thinkingSignature) {
        const reasoningItem = JSON.parse(block.thinkingSignature);
        output.push(reasoningItem); // keeps the original rs_... id
    }
}
```

candidates.text:
Make memory_extract fully async — eliminate double timeout

## Problem

`memory_extract` has a **double timeout** that causes data loss:

1. **External**: MCP gateway (30s) — kills the HTTP connection to memory-store-mcp
2. **Internal**: `generateTimeout = 120s` in `llm.go` — HTTP client timeout for Ollama call

Both are synchronous — `ExtractAndSave` calls `ExtractFacts` → `generateAnswer`, blocking the MCP handler. When text is long (e.g. full session conversation), the local qwen2.5-coder:7b on CPU (24 cores at 100%) can't finish in time, and facts are lost.

## Solution

Make `memory_extract` fully asynchronous:

- **MCP handler**: accepts text, pushes to worker queue, immediately returns `{status: "accepted"}`
- **Background worker**: calls `ExtractFacts` + `AsyncSave` with **no timeout limit**
- **Max 1 concurrent worker** — qwen2.5-coder:7b uses all 24 CPU cores at 100%
- **Optional**: job status endpoint (pending/done/failed)

## Changes needed

- `async.go` — new `AsyncExtractWorker` (job queue, 1 worker, sequential)
- `tools_extract.go` — `memory_extract` doesn't wait for result, pushes job
- `llm.go` — separate HTTP client for background calls without timeout; `--extract-model` flag for model selection

## Model note

Current model: `qwen2.5-coder:7b`. Do NOT swap without testing. Add `--extract-model` flag to allow testing `phi4-mini` vs `qwen2.5-coder:7b` on extraction quality.

candidates.text:
Make memory_extract fully async — eliminate double timeout

## Problem

`memory_extract` has a **double timeout** that causes data loss:

1. **External**: MCP gateway (30s) — kills the HTTP connection to memory-store-mcp
2. **Internal**: `generateTimeout = 120s` in `llm.go` — HTTP client timeout for Ollama call

Both are synchronous — `ExtractAndSave` calls `ExtractFacts` → `generateAnswer`, blocking the MCP handler. When text is long (e.g. full session conversation), the local qwen2.5-coder:7b on CPU (24 cores at 100%) can't finish in time, and facts are lost.

## Solution

Make `memory_extract` fully asynchronous:

- **MCP handler**: accepts text, pushes to worker queue, immediately returns `{status: "accepted"}`
- **Background worker**: calls `ExtractFacts` + `AsyncSave` with **no timeout limit**
- **Max 1 concurrent worker** — qwen2.5-coder:7b uses all 24 CPU cores at 100%
- **Optional**: job status endpoint (pending/done/failed)

## Changes needed

- `async.go` — new `AsyncExtractWorker` (job queue, 1 worker, sequential)
- `tools_extract.go` — `memory_extract` doesn't wait for result, pushes job
- `llm.go` — separate HTTP client for background calls without timeout; `--extract-model` flag for model selection

## Model note

Current model: `qwen2.5-coder:7b`. Do NOT swap without testing. Add `--extract-model` flag to allow testing `phi4-mini` vs `qwen2.5-coder:7b` on extraction quality.

candidates.text:
`JsonSchemaTransformer` skips `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` members when the node also has a `type`

### Initial Checks

- [x] I'm using the latest version of Pydantic AI (reproduced on `main` @ `3adb9b0`).
- [x] I've searched the issue tracker before opening this.

### Description

`JsonSchemaTransformer._handle` only recurses into `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` members when the node has no `type`:

```python
# pydantic_ai/_json_schema.py
elif type_ is None:
    schema = self._handle_union(schema, 'allOf')
    schema = self._handle_union(schema, 'anyOf')
    schema = self._handle_union(schema, 'oneOf')
```

`allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` are independent applicators: a node can legally carry both a `type` and one of them, and such nodes show up in practice via user-provided and MCP tool `inputSchema`s. When that happens, `_handle_object`/`_handle_array` recurse `properties`/`items` but never the composition members, so those members (and their nested subschemas) are never walked and `transform` is never applied to them. Provider transformers then leave provider-incompatible keys in place inside the members.

This is the same root family as #6394 (which added `allOf` recursion for the typeless case); it just is not reached when the node also has a `type`.

Invariant: every subschema in the tree should be visited by `transform` exactly once; `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` can co-exist with `type`.

### Minimal, Reproducible Example

Offline, no network or provider call:

```python
from pydantic_ai.profiles.google import GoogleJsonSchemaTransformer

schema = {
    'type': 'object',
    'properties': {'p': {'type': 'string'}},
    'anyOf': [
        {'type': 'integer', 'title': 'Count', 'exclusiveMinimum': 0},
    ],
}
out = GoogleJsonSchemaTransformer(schema).walk()
print(out['anyOf'][0])
# actual  : {'type': 'integer', 'title': 'Count', 'exclusiveMinimum': 0}
# expected: {'type': 'integer'}
```

### What happened?

Multi-turn conversations against `azure-openai-responses` reasoning models fail on the follow-up turn with:

```
400 Item with id 'rs_...' not found. Items are not persisted when store is set to false.
Try again with store set to true, or remove this item from your input.
```

This is the same class of failure as #4272 (Azure; closed as `closed-because-bigrefactor`, with fix PR #4256 never merged) and the OpenAI-side #3369 / #5059. It **still reproduces on 0.80.3 / current main** — the refactor did not close the Azure path.

**Root cause (code-grounded, 0.80.3):**

`packages/ai/src/api/openai-responses-shared.ts` → `convertResponsesMessages()` replays the captured reasoning item verbatim, including its server-side `rs_` id:

```js
if (block.type === "thinking") {
    if (block.thinkingSignature) {
        const reasoningItem = JSON.parse(block.thinkingSignature);
        output.push(reasoningItem); // keeps the original rs_... id

}
```

source_metadata.title: review hook: diff vs origin/<default> produces stale-base phantom-deletion findings on serially merged PRs

candidates.text:
review hook: diff vs origin/<default> produces stale-base phantom-deletion findings on serially merged PRs

## What happened

autumngarage/cortex#495 branched from main at commit `2bf1ada`. PR #494 then merged, adding `.cortex/journal/2026-06-09-pr-merged-pr493.md` and regenerating `state.md`. When #495 entered the merge gate, the review diffed the branch against `origin/main` (which now contained #494) and reported two **phantom findings**:

> - `.cortex/journal/2026-06-09-pr-merged-pr493.md:1` — deletes a tracked Journal entry, violating the append-only project-memory invariant
> - `.cortex/state.md:5` — generated state is rewound to an older HEAD/source set

Nothing was deleted or rewound — the branch simply predated #494. The reviewer correctly read the diff it was given; the diff itself was wrong for the question being asked. This is the recurring stale-base class (same shape as the sentinel #49/#50/#51 serial-merge incidents).

## Mitigation that worked

`gh api -X PUT repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/495/update-branch`, then rerun the gate → clean merge.

## Proposed fix (either layer works)

1. **Diff at the merge base**: review `git diff $(git merge-base origin/<default> HEAD)...HEAD` (triple-dot semantics) instead of `--base origin/<default>` two-dot, so already-merged sibling work never appears as deletions; or
2. **Auto-update before review**: when the branch is behind the base, call update-branch (or rebase in the worktree) before computing the review diff, failing visibly on conflicts; or at minimum
3. **Detect and instruct**: when behind-base is detected, prefix the review output with a stale-base warning and the update-branch command instead of letting phantom deletions reach the reviewer.

Serial merges of small PRs are the normal workflow under `open-pr.sh --auto-merge`; every PR after the first in a session is exposed to this class.

## 背景

对 milestone 33（Scheduled Agent-Key Credential v1）在 commit `34f336bd8f43adbd04714261105d2750c96c160a` 做验收复查后，确认核心链路已经实现：NyxID `full_key` 写入 Garnet secret vault，actor state / projection 只保存 `SecretReference`，执行时再现场解密。

关联：#2404、#2689、#2690。

### 1. vault `PutAsync` 失败后不会撤销已铸造的 NyxID key

`ScheduledAgentCreatorTool` 先调用 `IssueAsync`，再直接调用 mapper；`MapAsync` 内执行 vault `PutAsync`，但调用点没有异常补偿。若 Garnet 写入抛异常，NyxID key 会成为孤儿。

- `agents/Aevatar.GAgents.Authoring.Lark/ScheduledAgentCreatorTool.cs:185-193`
- `agents/Aevatar.GAgents.Authoring.Lark/ScheduledAgentCreateRequestMapper.cs:194-204`

### 2. vault 写入成功但 actor 初始化失败时，只撤销 NyxID key

initialize catch 只调用 `TryRevokeAsync(token, apiKeyId)`；已经写入的 vault reference 没有执行 `ISecretVault.RevokeAsync`，加密记录仍可解析直到过期或人工清理。

- `agents/Aevatar.GAgents.Authoring.Lark/ScheduledAgentCreatorTool.cs:196-204`

### 3. 删除 scheduled agent 时没有执行双轨撤销

删除流程 tombstone 后仅调用 NyxID DELETE/outbox。catalog revocation 事实中已经携带 `NyxApiKeyReference`，但删除链路没有消费该 reference 执行本地 vault revoke。

- `agents/Aevatar.GAgents.Authoring.Lark/AgentBuilderTool.cs:261-281`
- `agents/Aevatar.GAgents.Scheduled/UserAgentCatalogGAgent.cs:418-429`

### 4. 出站 allowlist 派生失败时仍 fail-open

owner LLM config 查询异常后，issuer 返回 `null` 并继续铸造不含 LLM route grant 的 key，让失败延迟到定时运行时 403；这与 #2690 的“出站面无法解析时 fail closed 拒绝铸 key”不一致。

- `agents/Aevatar.GAgents.Authoring.Lark/ScheduledAgentApiKeyIssuer.cs:206-223`

`ScheduledAgentApiKeyIssueResult.FullKey` 已有 `[JsonIgnore]` 且 `ToString()` 打码，但仍是公开 record 属性，不满足 #2690 约定的不可序列化 opaque holder；其他 serializer、反射、record copy/deconstruction 仍可传播该值。

Azure OpenAI Responses (store:false) still 400s on multi-turn reasoning replay in 0.80.3 (bare rs_ id, no encrypted_content backfill)

### What happened?

Multi-turn conversations against `azure-openai-responses` reasoning models fail on the follow-up turn with:

```
400 Item with id 'rs_...' not found. Items are not persisted when store is set to false.
Try again with store set to true, or remove this item from your input.
```

This is the same class of failure as #4272 (Azure; closed as `closed-because-bigrefactor`, with fix PR #4256 never merged) and the OpenAI-side #3369 / #5059. It **still reproduces on 0.80.3 / current main** — the refactor did not close the Azure path.

**Root cause (code-grounded, 0.80.3):**

`packages/ai/src/api/openai-responses-shared.ts` → `convertResponsesMessages()` replays the captured reasoning item verbatim, including its server-side `rs_` id:

```js
if (block.type === "thinking") {
    if (block.thinkingSignature) {
        const reasoningItem = JSON.parse(block.thinkingSignature);
        output.push(reasoningItem); // keeps the original rs_... id
    }
}
```

`packages/ai/src/api/azure-openai-responses.ts` sends `store: false`, and requests `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]` **only** when a reasoning effort/summary is set; there is **no backfill** of `encrypted_content` from the final `response.completed.response.output[]`.

When the captured reasoning item ends up without `encrypted_content` (per #4272, Azure does not always populate it on the intermediate `response.output_item.done`), the next turn's `input` carries a **bare `rs_` id**. Under `store: false` the server persists nothing, so the lookup fails → 400.

The tool-call path has the same shape: the `fc_` item id is omitted only for cross-model replay (`isDifferentModel`), not for same-model Azure under `store: false`.

## Problem

The repository already runs PMD's Copy/Paste Detector (CPD) as part of
`./mvnw -q spotless:check verify`. CPD keeps exact and token-level copy/paste duplication from
growing, but it is not intended to find every renamed, reordered, structurally similar, or more

refactoring of genuine duplication. The objective is less duplicated behavior and maintenance work,
not merely another green CI job.

Other — static analysis and maintainability.

Evaluate and integrate one reproducible clone detector that complements CPD, then use its findings to
reduce justified duplication in production and test code.

[`stonedetector/stonedetector` Docker image](https://hub.docker.com/r/stonedetector/stonedetector).

candidates.text:
Support per-tool strict schema passthrough in defineTool

### What problem are you trying to solve?

The AI SDK supports a per-tool `strict?: boolean` flag for function tools, and OpenAI-compatible providers can forward it as `tools[].function.strict`. Eve currently has no public or compiled representation for that flag:

- `ToolDefinition` / `PublicToolDefinition` do not expose `strict`.
- `InternalToolDefinition` and `CompiledToolDefinition` do not carry it.
- The compiled manifest schema has no `strict` field for tools.

As a result, an authored Eve tool cannot opt into provider-native strict tool calling. Adding `strict: true` behind a cast is not sufficient because the compiler/runtime boundary does not preserve the field.

Minimal API shape that is currently unavailable:

```ts
import { defineTool } from "eve/tools";
```

`JsonSchemaTransformer` skips `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` members when the node also has a `type`

### Initial Checks

- [x] I'm using the latest version of Pydantic AI (reproduced on `main` @ `3adb9b0`).
- [x] I've searched the issue tracker before opening this.

### Description

`JsonSchemaTransformer._handle` only recurses into `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` members when the node has no `type`:

```python
# pydantic_ai/_json_schema.py
elif type_ is None:
    schema = self._handle_union(schema, 'allOf')
    schema = self._handle_union(schema, 'anyOf')
    schema = self._handle_union(schema, 'oneOf')
```

`allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` are independent applicators: a node can legally carry both a `type` and one of them, and such nodes show up in practice via user-provided and MCP tool `inputSchema`s. When that happens, `_handle_object`/`_handle_array` recurse `properties`/`items` but never the composition members, so those members (and their nested subschemas) are never walked and `transform` is never applied to them. Provider transformers then leave provider-incompatible keys in place inside the members.

This is the same root family as #6394 (which added `allOf` recursion for the typeless case); it just is not reached when the node also has a `type`.

Invariant: every subschema in the tree should be visited by `transform` exactly once; `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` can co-exist with `type`.

### Minimal, Reproducible Example

Offline, no network or provider call:

```python
from pydantic_ai.profiles.google import GoogleJsonSchemaTransformer

schema = {
    'type': 'object',
    'properties': {'p': {'type': 'string'}},
    'anyOf': [
        {'type': 'integer', 'title': 'Count', 'exclusiveMinimum': 0},
    ],
}
out = GoogleJsonSchemaTransformer(schema).walk()
print(out['anyOf'][0])
# actual  : {'type': 'integer', 'title': 'Count', 'exclusiveMinimum': 0}
# expected: {'type': 'integer'}
```

### What happened?

Multi-turn conversations against `azure-openai-responses` reasoning models fail on the follow-up turn with:

```
400 Item with id 'rs_...' not found. Items are not persisted when store is set to false.
Try again with store set to true, or remove this item from your input.
```

This is the same class of failure as #4272 (Azure; closed as `closed-because-bigrefactor`, with fix PR #4256 never merged) and the OpenAI-side #3369 / #5059. It **still reproduces on 0.80.3 / current main** — the refactor did not close the Azure path.

**Root cause (code-grounded, 0.80.3):**

`packages/ai/src/api/openai-responses-shared.ts` → `convertResponsesMessages()` replays the captured reasoning item verbatim, including its server-side `rs_` id:

```js
if (block.type === "thinking") {
    if (block.thinkingSignature) {
        const reasoningItem = JSON.parse(block.thinkingSignature);
        output.push(reasoningItem); // keeps the original rs_... id
```

Explore an MCP server for QCobro

## Summary
Investigate exposing QCobro's capabilities via a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so AI agents/tools can interact with the platform programmatically.

## Problem / Motivation
QCobro already has a solid, well-typed API (tRPC over `mods/apiserver`, contracts shared via `mods/common`). As AI agents (including coding/ops agents) and external tooling increasingly rely on MCP as the standard way to interact with services, QCobro currently has no MCP surface — any agent-driven workflow (querying campaigns, contacts, payment promises, gestiones, or triggering outreach) requires bespoke integration instead of a discoverable, standard interface.

## Proposed Solution
Explore wrapping/exposing existing tRPC procedures as MCP tools/resources. Key open questions to research:
- **Architecture**: where the MCP server would live (new `mods/mcp` package vs. a thin layer in `mods/apiserver`) and how it reuses `mods/common` schemas/types rather than duplicating contracts.
- **Auth model**: introduce a dedicated, limited-permission role/scope (via Fonoster Identity) for MCP access, distinct from full operator permissions, so agent-driven actions are scoped down by default (e.g. read-only or a narrow allowlist of mutations).
- **Scope of exposed operations**: which are safe to expose first (read-heavy: contacts, campaigns, payment promises, gestiones) vs. which are too risky for unsupervised agent-initiated writes (e.g. dispatching outreach, marking payments paid).
- **Auditability**: rate limiting and audit logging for MCP-originated actions, since they may be less supervised than operator UI actions.
- **Multi-tenancy**: whether this is a single general MCP server or workspace-scoped, given QCobro's multi-tenant model.
